question: What does a healthy healing wound bed look like when it's doing well?
explanation: You're doing great! Healthy healing tissue (granulation tissue) is packed with fresh blood vessels, giving it a bright red, shiny, and moist look that shows healing is well underway.

question: Why do nurses check the skin right around a wound (the periwound area), not just the wound itself?

options.A: It determines how much protein the patient needs in their diet.
options.B: It dictates the exact brand of dressing the doctor must prescribe.
options.C: It shows if drainage or moisture is damaging the healthy skin around the wound.
options.D: It helps calculate the exact surface area in square centimeters.

explanation: Spotting issues early around the wound helps you catch irritation or moisture damage before the wound starts getting bigger. You've got this!

question: What level of technique is normally used when changing chronic wound dressings at home?
explanation: For routine home care, clean technique is the standard! It relies on solid hand hygiene and clean tools rather than trying to keep things operating-room sterile.

question: Which of these is NOT a good step when setting up a clean workspace on a household table?

options.A: Washing your hands thoroughly before touching any supplies
options.B: Using a clean disposable barrier like a paper towel as your work surface
options.C: Keeping clean supplies separate from used or dirty items
options.D: Spraying the table with a standard household bleach solution right before laying down sterile instruments

explanation: Spray bottles and wet chemicals right next to open supplies can easily contaminate your clean field. Using a dry paper towel barrier is much safer!

question: Which dressing works best for a wound that has heavy bleeding or fluid drainage?
explanation: Alginates come from seaweed and are superstars at soaking up lots of fluid while turning into a soft gel that keeps the wound bed happy.

question: When packing a deep wound in a patient's home, what is the golden rule for placing the gauze inside?

options.A: Pack the wound tightly until it is completely firm to stop all bleeding.
options.B: Pack the wound loosely so it fills the space without putting pressure on the tissue.
options.C: Pack the wound using dry cotton balls for maximum absorption.
options.D: Pack only the top layer of skin and leave the deeper cavity empty.

explanation: Remember: never pack too tightly! Packing a wound too firmly cuts off the blood supply those new cells need to heal.

question: What should you do first if an old sticky dressing won't budge from a wound bed?

options.A: Moisten it slightly with sterile saline to loosen it gently
options.B: Soak the entire limb in a bucket of tap water
options.C: Cut the skin around the tape to remove it
options.D: Pull it off quickly in one sharp motion to save time

explanation: A little saline goes a long way. Moistening a stuck dressing protects delicate new tissue and keeps your patient comfortable.

question: Why do nurses clean a wound starting from the center and wiping outward?

options.A: It makes the cleaning solution spread evenly across the room.
options.B: It stops the patient from feeling ticklish during the procedure.
options.C: It speeds up how fast the skin cells can multiply.
options.D: It prevents pushing bacteria from the surrounding skin back into the wound bed.

explanation: Think of the center as the cleanest zone. Wiping outward ensures you don't drag outside germs back into the healing tissue!

question: Which sign clearly points to a worsening wound infection?

options.A: Mild itching around the edge of the tape
options.B: Firm, pink tissue filling the wound base
options.C: Foul-smelling, purulent drainage and spreading redness
options.D: A thin layer of clear, watery fluid on the surface

explanation: Pus, a bad smell, and redness that creeps outward are classic red flags that bacteria are taking over and causing an active infection.

question: A patient's abdominal surgical wound suddenly pops open and loop of bowel peeks out. What is your immediate action?

options.A: Apply an ice pack to the exposed tissue to reduce swelling
options.B: Wait until the scheduled doctor appointment next week to report it
options.C: Cover the area with sterile saline-moistened dressings and call for emergency help
options.D: Gently push the bowel back inside the abdomen and tape it shut

explanation: This is an emergency called evisceration! Keep the organs moist with sterile saline dressings and call for emergency help right away—never push them back in.

question: Why is a 'return demonstration' the best way to see if a family caregiver knows how to do a dressing change?

options.A: It replaces the need to document anything in the patient chart.
options.B: It allows the nurse to leave the home early while the family works.
options.C: It ensures the family buys the most expensive medical supplies.
options.D: It proves they can physically perform the steps correctly rather than just nodding yes.

explanation: Seeing is believing! Having them do it in front of you ensures they really understand the steps, way better than just taking their word for it.

question: What is the main role of a home care nurse when working with the healthcare team on a slow-healing wound?

options.A: Acting as the eyes and ears to report accurate, up-to-date wound changes to providers
options.B: Ordering all prescription medications without physician approval
options.C: Performing surgical debridement during every home visit
options.D: Diagnosing the underlying systemic disease independently

explanation: You are the vital link! Your accurate updates from the home help doctors, dietitians, and specialists adjust the care plan so the patient heals faster.
